title: Small vs. Large Energy Surplus for Hypertrophy and Body Composition (Helms et al.)
content: Helms et al. — Comparing a smaller vs. larger calorie surplus during a structured resistance-training muscle-gain phase: a smaller, more conservative surplus tends to produce a more favorable ratio of lean mass gain to fat mass gain than a large surplus, which mainly accelerates fat gain without a proportional increase in muscle-gain rate once training-driven hypertrophy capacity is roughly met.

title: Small vs. Large Energy Surplus for Hypertrophy and Body Composition (Helms et al.)
content: Helms et al. — Product implication: a conservative surplus (commonly cited product-heuristic range of roughly 5-15% above maintenance, or ~200-300 kcal/day for most recreational lifters) is a more defensible default starting point than an aggressive surplus; a large surplus should be flagged to the user as increasing fat-gain risk without a matched increase in muscle-gain benefit, consistent with this codebase's own CONSERVATIVE_SURPLUS_PCT / LARGE_SURPLUS_WARNING_PCT config.
